title: The manifest and the stale rule

keeps.check: Make a scratch consumer repository with a main branch, a dprint.jsonc copied from this repository, and a .config/bootstrap.toml with environments = ["dev"], [tools.python] and a pyproject.toml at the root. Set SYNC_ENGINE_CACHE to a scratch folder, SYNC_ENGINE_URL to a local clone of the run's branch and REPO_SYNC_NO_AUTOUPDATE=1 for every step. Run mise run setup:configs in it (use MISE_TRUSTED_CONFIG_PATHS and symlinks of gomplate, dprint and pre-commit in a scratch bin folder on PATH, as the K1 run of the repo-sync-check plan did). Commit the result. Then remove [tools.python] and the pyproject.toml, and run mise run setup:configs again.
keeps.pass: The first run exits 0 and writes .config/repo-generated.tsv: its first line is the comment line, its rows are sorted, it lists .config/mise/conf.d/python/mise.dev.toml and no seed. The second run exits 0, removes each python file that has the header (the conf.d/python folder goes too, when empty), keeps every file without the header, and writes a manifest without python rows.

after_landing.notes: Archives the plan folder only when its gaps list has no open entry; with an open gap, skip this step and leave the folder live.

release_levels.reason: The sync writes a new committed file .config/repo-generated.tsv and removes stale synced files from it. This is new behavior; a consumer changes nothing but a commit of the new file.

units.title: Engine: the manifest library and the repo stale rule
Tests: the manifest and the stale rule
units.waits: Its cases run the manifest code that U1 writes in sync-engine/manifest and sync-engine/repo-sync.

shared_files.why: every human-facing doc; the earlier units report DOCS FALSIFIED lines and never edit a doc

decisions.decision: Does the plan need a review unit?
decisions.ruling: Yes. U1 changes sync-engine/repo-sync and adds sync-engine/manifest, and U2 changes a test task. Both are runnable bash, and the stale rule deletes files. One review unit in wave 3 covers U1 and U2.
decisions.rejected: No review unit; the wave review alone does not run /security-review.

decisions.decision: Why is this plan in one linear chain with the other plans of the merge?
decisions.ruling: The 16 plans form one linear chain through requires. Most of them edit sync-engine/repo-sync or sync-engine/setup-sync, and parallel plans conflict there.

decisions.decision: Where do the tests of the new rules go?
decisions.ruling: This plan extends test:repo-sync with cases for its new rules. An existing case changes only where a ruling changes its expected result.

decisions.decision: Who runs mise run setup:configs in bootstrap and in the consumers?
decisions.ruling: The user, by hand, after the landing. It is out of scope, as in the earlier plans.
decisions.rejected: A unit or an after-landing step runs setup:configs.

decisions.decision: What does the first sync with no manifest remove?
decisions.ruling: Nothing. The first sync has no manifest and removes nothing. docs/sync/migrate.md lists the old leftovers, and the owner deletes them by hand as before.
decisions.rejected: A one-time header scan of the repository, which needs a guard for the own sources of bootstrap.

decisions.decision: Does a run with a failure remove stale files?
decisions.ruling: No. The stale removal and the manifest write run only after a run without a failure, in this order: stale removal, manifest write, bootstrap_commit. A failed removal is a failure, so the manifest is not written and the next clean run tries again.
decisions.rejected: Remove stale files also after a failure, with the paths of the failed files as a guard (today _RS_SEEN); a failed file then looks stale.

decisions.decision: Which manifest rows does the stale rule refuse?
decisions.ruling: The manifest is a committed file of the consumer, so the engine does not trust it. A row without a TAB, with an empty tool or path, with an absolute path, or with a .. segment is skipped with a log line and never removed. A listed path that is a symlink, or that has a symlinked folder between the target root and the file, is not removed (repo-sync never follows a link).
decisions.rejected: Remove each listed path as it is.

decisions.decision: What does a dry run do with the manifest?
decisions.ruling: A dry run prints would remove <path> for each stale file and would write .config/repo-generated.tsv when the new content differs from the file. It writes and removes nothing. A real run writes the manifest only when its content changes.
decisions.rejected: A dry run prints nothing about the manifest.

decisions.decision: What happens to the removal of the merge tasks of the other branch model (_RS_SKIP and _rs_remove)?
decisions.ruling: It stays as it is. It is a rule of the branch model and works also without a manifest. The stale rule replaces only _rs_stale and the removal in _rs_skip_required.
decisions.rejected: Remove it and let the stale rule remove the merge tasks; a repository without a manifest then keeps both models.

decisions.decision: Which rows does a clean run write?
decisions.ruling: One row <tool><TAB><path> for each file of mode generated that the run writes or finds unchanged, and for each generated conf.d mise file. A seed, a merge file, a skipped file (an environment that the repo does not use, a requires or requires_found file that is not present) and a removed merge task have no row. The path is relative to MISE_PROJECT_ROOT, without .tmpl.
decisions.rejected: List every file that the tool ships, also the skipped ones.

decisions.decision: Which paths does the stale rule spare?
decisions.ruling: Every path that this run handled: each generated, seed and merge file that the run wrote or kept. Only a listed path that the run did not handle is a candidate for removal.

decisions.decision: What does the stale rule do with a merge task of the other branch model?
decisions.ruling: The stale rule skips the paths in _RS_SKIP, because _rs_remove already removes them. A dry run logs one would remove line for each file.
decisions.rejected: Accept the duplicate would remove line.

decisions.decision: What is the exact byte form of the manifest?
decisions.ruling: LF line endings, no trailing blanks, and exactly one LF at the end, so the pre-commit hooks never rewrite it.
decisions.rejected: Any line form that the reader accepts.

decisions.decision: How does the stale rule treat symlinks on the two sides?
decisions.ruling: sync-engine/manifest takes a link mode. repo: a path that is a symlink, or under a symlinked folder, is never removed (D7). macos: the stale rule resolves links and removes the real file, then prunes empty parents up to the target root ($HOME), never past a symlinked folder (the rule of setup-sync), because on the Mac ~/.config/mise is a link into the dotfiles/ of the owner, and the mise config of a deselected tool must go.
decisions.rejected: One link rule for both sides.
